9878.text: For he had not left to Je·hoʹa·haz any people but fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand men on foot, because the king of Syria had destroyed them, that he might make them like the dust at threshing.

9879.label: 2 Kings 13:8
9879.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Je·hoʹa·haz and all that he did and his mightiness, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9880.label: 2 Kings 13:9
9880.text: Finally Je·hoʹa·haz lay down with his forefathers, and they buried him in Sa·marʹi·a; and Je·hoʹash his son began to reign in place of him.

9881.label: 2 Kings 13:10
9881.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Je·hoʹash the king of Judah, Je·hoʹash the son of Je·hoʹa·haz became king over Israel in Sa·marʹi·a for sixteen years.

9882.label: 2 Kings 13:11
9882.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. He did not depart from all the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, with which he made Israel sin. In them he walked.

9883.label: 2 Kings 13:12
9883.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Je·hoʹash and all that he did and his mightiness [and] how he fought against Am·a·ziʹah the king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9884.label: 2 Kings 13:13
9884.text: Finally Je·hoʹash lay down with his forefathers, and Jer·o·boʹam himself sat upon his throne. In turn Je·hoʹash was buried in Sa·marʹi·a with the kings of Israel.

9885.label: 2 Kings 13:14
9885.text: As regards E·liʹsha, he had taken sick with the sickness with which he was to die. So Je·hoʹash the king of Israel came down to him and began to weep over his face and say: “My father, my father, the war chariot of Israel and his horsemen!”

9886.label: 2 Kings 13:15
9886.text: And E·liʹsha proceeded to say to him: “Take a bow and arrows.” So he took to himself a bow and arrows.

9887.label: 2 Kings 13:16
9887.text: And he went on to say to the king of Israel: “Put your hand to the bow.” Accordingly he put his hand to it, after which E·liʹsha laid his hands upon the hands of the king.

9888.label: 2 Kings 13:17
9888.text: Then he said: “Open the window to the east.” So he opened it. Finally E·liʹsha said: “Shoot!” So he shot. He now said: “Jehovah’s arrow of salvation, even the arrow of salvation against Syria! And you will certainly strike down Syria at Aʹphek to the finishing point.”

9889.label: 2 Kings 13:18
9889.text: And he went on to say: “Take the arrows.” At that he took [them]. Then he said to the king of Israel: “Strike on the earth.” So he struck three times and stopped.

9890.label: 2 Kings 13:19
9890.text: And the man of the [true] God grew indignant at him; hence he said: “It was meant to strike five or six times! In that case you would certainly be striking down Syria to the finishing point, but now it is three times that you will strike down Syria.”

9891.label: 2 Kings 13:20
9891.text: After that E·liʹsha died and they buried him. And there were marauding bands of the Moʹab·ites that regularly came into the land at the coming in of the year.

9892.label: 2 Kings 13:21
9892.text: And it came about that as they were burying a man, why, here they saw the marauding band. At once they threw the man into E·liʹsha’s burial place and went off. When the man touched the bones of E·liʹsha, he immediately came to life and stood upon his feet.

9893.label: 2 Kings 13:22
9893.text: As for Hazʹa·el the king of Syria, he oppressed Israel all the days of Je·hoʹa·haz.

9894.label: 2 Kings 13:23
9894.text: However, Jehovah showed them favor and had mercy upon them and turned to them for the sake of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; and he did not want to bring them to ruin, and he did not cast them away from before his face until now.

9895.label: 2 Kings 13:24
9895.text: Finally Hazʹa·el the king of Syria died, and Ben-haʹdad his son began to reign in place of him.

9896.label: 2 Kings 13:25
9896.text: And Je·hoʹash the son of Je·hoʹa·haz proceeded to take back again from the hand of Ben-haʹdad the son of Hazʹa·el the cities that he had taken from the hand of Je·hoʹa·haz his father in war. Three times Je·hoʹash struck him down, and he got to recover the cities of Israel.

9897.label: 2 Kings 14:1
9897.text: In the second year of Je·hoʹash the son of Je·hoʹa·haz the king of Israel, Am·a·ziʹah the son of Je·hoʹash the king of Judah became king.

9898.label: 2 Kings 14:2
9898.text: Twenty-five years old he happened to be when he began to reign, and for twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Je·ho·adʹdin of Jerusalem.

9899.label: 2 Kings 14:3
9899.text: And he continued to do what was upright in Jehovah’s eyes, only not like David his forefather. According to all that Je·hoʹash his father had done, he did.

9900.label: 2 Kings 14:4
9900.text: It was only the high places that did not disappear. The people were still sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on the high places.

9901.label: 2 Kings 14:5
9901.text: And it came about that as soon as the kingdom had become firm in his hand, he began to strike down his servants that had struck down the king his father.

9902.label: 2 Kings 14:6
9902.text: And the sons of the strikers he did not put to death, according to what is written in the book of Moses’ law that Jehovah gave in command, saying: “Fathers should not be put to death for sons, and sons themselves should not be put to death for fathers; but for his own sin should each one be put to death.”

9903.label: 2 Kings 14:7
9903.text: He himself struck down the Eʹdom·ites in the Valley of Salt, ten thousand men, and got to seize Seʹla in the war, and its name came to be called Jokʹthe·el down to this day.

9904.label: 2 Kings 14:8
9904.text: Then it was that Am·a·ziʹah sent messengers to Je·hoʹash the son of Je·hoʹa·haz the son of Jeʹhu the king of Israel, saying: “Do come. Let us look each other in the face.”

9905.label: 2 Kings 14:9
9905.text: At that Je·hoʹash the king of Israel sent to Am·a·ziʹah the king of Judah, saying: “The thorny weed itself that was in Lebʹa·non sent to the cedar that was in Lebʹa·non, saying, ‘Do give your daughter to my son as a wife.’ However, a wild beast of the field that was in Lebʹa·non passed by and trampled the thorny weed down.

9906.label: 2 Kings 14:10
9906.text: You have unmistakably struck down Eʹdom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy your honor and dwell in your own house. Why, then, should you engage in strife under unfavorable conditions and have to fall, you and Judah with you?”

9907.label: 2 Kings 14:11
9907.text: And Am·a·ziʹah did not listen. So Je·hoʹash the king of Israel came up, and they proceeded to look each other in the face, he and Am·a·ziʹah the king of Judah, at Beth-sheʹmesh, which belongs to Judah.

9908.label: 2 Kings 14:12
9908.text: And Judah came to be defeated before Israel, so that they took to flight, each one to his tent.

9909.label: 2 Kings 14:13
9909.text: And it was Am·a·ziʹah the king of Judah the son of Je·hoʹash the son of A·ha·ziʹah that Je·hoʹash the king of Israel captured at Beth-sheʹmesh, after which they came to Jerusalem and he made a breach in the wall of Jerusalem at the Gate of Eʹphra·im clear to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

9910.label: 2 Kings 14:14
9910.text: And he took all the gold and silver and all the articles to be found at the house of Jehovah and in the treasures of the house of the king and the hostages and then returned to Sa·marʹi·a.

9911.label: 2 Kings 14:15
9911.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Je·hoʹash, what he did and his mightiness and how he fought against Am·a·ziʹah the king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9912.label: 2 Kings 14:16
9912.text: Finally Je·hoʹash lay down with his forefathers and was buried in Sa·marʹi·a with the kings of Israel, and Jer·o·boʹam his son began to reign in place of him.

9913.label: 2 Kings 14:17
9913.text: And Am·a·ziʹah the son of Je·hoʹash the king of Judah continued to live after the death of Je·hoʹash the son of Je·hoʹa·haz the king of Israel for fifteen years.

9914.label: 2 Kings 14:18
9914.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Am·a·ziʹah, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

9915.label: 2 Kings 14:19
9915.text: At length they leagued against him in a conspiracy at Jerusalem, and he went fleeing to Laʹchish; but they sent in pursuit of him to Laʹchish and put him to death there.

9916.label: 2 Kings 14:20
9916.text: So they carried him upon horses and he was buried in Jerusalem with his forefathers in the City of David.

9917.label: 2 Kings 14:21
9917.text: Then all the people of Judah took Az·a·riʹah, he at the time being sixteen years old, and they made him king in place of his father Am·a·ziʹah.

9918.label: 2 Kings 14:22
9918.text: He himself built Eʹlath and got to restore it to Judah after the king lay down with his forefathers.

9919.label: 2 Kings 14:23
9919.text: In the fifteenth year of Am·a·ziʹah the son of Je·hoʹash the king of Judah, Jer·o·boʹam the son of Je·hoʹash the king of Israel became king in Sa·marʹi·a for forty-one years.

9920.label: 2 Kings 14:24
9920.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. He did not depart from all the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, with which he caused Israel to sin.

9921.label: 2 Kings 14:25
9921.text: He it was that restored the boundary of Israel from the entering in of Haʹmath clear to the sea of the Arʹa·bah, according to the word of Jehovah the God of Israel who spoke by means of his servant Joʹnah the son of A·mitʹtai, the prophet that was from Gath-heʹpher.

9922.label: 2 Kings 14:26
9922.text: For Jehovah had seen the very bitter affliction of Israel. There was neither any helpless one nor any worthless one, nor was there a helper for Israel.

9923.label: 2 Kings 14:27
9923.text: And Jehovah had promised not to wipe out the name of Israel from under the heavens. Consequently he saved them by the hand of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Je·hoʹash.

9924.label: 2 Kings 14:28
9924.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Jer·o·boʹam and all that he did and his mightiness, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Haʹmath to Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9925.label: 2 Kings 14:29
9925.text: Finally Jer·o·boʹam lay down with his forefathers, with the kings of Israel, and Zech·a·riʹah his son began to reign in place of him.

9926.label: 2 Kings 15:1
9926.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Jer·o·boʹam the king of Israel, Az·a·riʹah the son of Am·a·ziʹah the king of Judah became king.

9927.label: 2 Kings 15:2
9927.text: Sixteen years old he happened to be when he began to reign, and for fifty-two years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Je·co·liʹah of Jerusalem.

9928.label: 2 Kings 15:3
9928.text: And he continued to do what was upright in Jehovah’s eyes, according to all that Am·a·ziʹah his father had done.

9929.label: 2 Kings 15:4
9929.text: It was only that the high places did not disappear. The people were still sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on the high places.

9930.label: 2 Kings 15:5
9930.text: Finally Jehovah plagued the king, and he continued to be a leper until the day of his death, and he kept dwelling in his house exempt from duties, while Joʹtham the king’s son was over the house, judging the people of the land.

9931.label: 2 Kings 15:6
9931.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Az·a·riʹah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

9932.label: 2 Kings 15:7
9932.text: At length Az·a·riʹah lay down with his forefathers, and they buried him with his forefathers in the City of David; and Joʹtham his son began to reign in place of him.

9933.label: 2 Kings 15:8
9933.text: In the thirty-eighth year of Az·a·riʹah the king of Judah, Zech·a·riʹah the son of Jer·o·boʹam became king over Israel in Sa·marʹi·a for six months.

9934.label: 2 Kings 15:9
9934.text: And he went on doing what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, just as his forefathers had done. He did not depart from the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, with which he caused Israel to sin.

9935.label: 2 Kings 15:10
9935.text: Then Shalʹlum the son of Jaʹbesh conspired against him and struck him down at Ibʹle·am and put him to death and began to reign in place of him.

9936.label: 2 Kings 15:11
9936.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Zech·a·riʹah, there they are written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel.

9937.label: 2 Kings 15:12
9937.text: That was Jehovah’s word that he had spoken to Jeʹhu, saying: “Sons themselves to the fourth generation will sit for you upon the throne of Israel.” And it came to be that way.

9938.label: 2 Kings 15:13
9938.text: As for Shalʹlum the son of Jaʹbesh, he became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uz·ziʹah the king of Judah, and he continued to reign for a full lunar month in Sa·marʹi·a.

9939.label: 2 Kings 15:14
9939.text: Then Menʹa·hem the son of Gaʹdi came up from Tirʹzah and came to Sa·marʹi·a and struck down Shalʹlum the son of Jaʹbesh in Sa·marʹi·a and put him to death; and he began to reign in place of him.

9940.label: 2 Kings 15:15
9940.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Shalʹlum and his conspiracy with which he conspired, there they are written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel.

9941.label: 2 Kings 15:16
9941.text: It was then that Menʹa·hem proceeded to strike down Tiphʹsah and all that was in it and its territory out from Tirʹzah, because it did not open up, and he went striking it down. All its pregnant women he ripped up.

9942.label: 2 Kings 15:17
9942.text: In the thirty-ninth year of Az·a·riʹah the king of Judah, Menʹa·hem the son of Gaʹdi became king over Israel for ten years in Sa·marʹi·a.

9943.label: 2 Kings 15:18
9943.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. He did not depart from all the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, with which he caused Israel to sin, all his days.

9944.label: 2 Kings 15:19
9944.text: Pul the king of As·syrʹi·a came into the land. Consequently Menʹa·hem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hands might prove to be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his own hand.

9945.label: 2 Kings 15:20
9945.text: So Menʹa·hem brought forth the silver at the expense of Israel, at the expense of all the valiant, mighty men, to give to the king of As·syrʹi·a fifty silver shekels for each man. At that the king of As·syrʹi·a turned back, and he did not stay there in the land.

9946.label: 2 Kings 15:21
9946.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Menʹa·hem and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel?

9947.label: 2 Kings 15:22
9947.text: Finally Menʹa·hem lay down with his forefathers, and Pek·a·hiʹah his son began to reign in place of him.

9948.label: 2 Kings 15:23
9948.text: In the fiftieth year of Az·a·riʹah the king of Judah, Pek·a·hiʹah the son of Menʹa·hem became king over Israel in Sa·marʹi·a for two years.

9949.label: 2 Kings 15:24
9949.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. He did not depart from the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, with which he caused Israel to sin.

9950.label: 2 Kings 15:25
9950.text: Then Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah his adjutant conspired against him and struck him down in Sa·marʹi·a in the dwelling tower of the king’s house with Arʹgob and A·riʹeh, and with him there were fifty men of the sons of Gilʹe·ad. So he put him to death and began to reign in place of him.

9951.label: 2 Kings 15:26
9951.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Pek·a·hiʹah and all that he did, there they are written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel.

9952.label: 2 Kings 15:27
9952.text: In the fifty-second year of Az·a·riʹah the king of Judah, Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah became king over Israel in Sa·marʹi·a for twenty years.

9953.label: 2 Kings 15:28
9953.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes. He did not depart from the sins of Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, with which he caused Israel to sin.

9954.label: 2 Kings 15:29
9954.text: In the days of Peʹkah the king of Israel, Tigʹlath-pil·eʹser the king of As·syrʹi·a came in and proceeded to take Iʹjon and Aʹbel-beth-maʹa·cah and Ja·noʹah and Keʹdesh and Haʹzor and Gilʹe·ad and Galʹi·lee, all the land of Naphʹta·li, and to carry them into exile in As·syrʹi·a.

9955.label: 2 Kings 15:30
9955.text: Finally Ho·sheʹa the son of Eʹlah formed a conspiracy against Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah and struck him and put him to death; and he began to reign in place of him in the twentieth year of Joʹtham the son of Uz·ziʹah.

9956.label: 2 Kings 15:31
9956.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Peʹkah and all that he did, there they are written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Israel.

9957.label: 2 Kings 15:32
9957.text: In the second year of Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah the king of Israel, Joʹtham the son of Uz·ziʹah the king of Judah became king.

9958.label: 2 Kings 15:33
9958.text: Twenty-five years old he happened to be when he began to reign, and for sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Je·ruʹsha the daughter of Zaʹdok.

9959.label: 2 Kings 15:34
9959.text: And he continued to do what was right in Jehovah’s eyes. According to all that Uz·ziʹah his father had done, he did.

9960.label: 2 Kings 15:35
9960.text: It was only that the high places did not disappear. The people were still sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on the high places. He it was that built the upper gate of the house of Jehovah.

9961.label: 2 Kings 15:36
9961.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Joʹtham, what he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

9962.label: 2 Kings 15:37
9962.text: In those days Jehovah started to send against Judah Reʹzin the king of Syria and Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah.

9963.label: 2 Kings 15:38
9963.text: Finally Joʹtham lay down with his forefathers and was buried with his forefathers in the City of David his forefather; and Aʹhaz his son began to reign in place of him.

9964.label: 2 Kings 16:1
9964.text: In the seventeenth year of Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah, Aʹhaz the son of Joʹtham the king of Judah became king.

9965.label: 2 Kings 16:2
9965.text: Twenty years old was Aʹhaz when he began to reign, and for sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was right in the eyes of Jehovah his God like David his forefather.

9966.label: 2 Kings 16:3
9966.text: And he went walking in the way of the kings of Israel, and even his own son he made pass through the fire, according to the detestable things of the nations whom Jehovah drove out because of the sons of Israel.

9967.label: 2 Kings 16:4
9967.text: And he kept sacrificing and making sacrificial smoke on the high places and upon the hills and under every luxuriant tree.

9968.label: 2 Kings 16:5
9968.text: It was then that Reʹzin the king of Syria and Peʹkah the son of Rem·a·liʹah the king of Israel proceeded to come up against Jerusalem in war and laid siege against Aʹhaz, but they were not able to fight.

9969.label: 2 Kings 16:6
9969.text: At that time Reʹzin the king of Syria restored Eʹlath to Eʹdom, after which he cleared out the Jews from Eʹlath; and the Eʹdom·ites, for their part, entered Eʹlath and kept dwelling there down to this day.

9970.label: 2 Kings 16:7
9970.text: So Aʹhaz sent messengers to Tigʹlath-pil·eʹser the king of As·syrʹi·a, saying: “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me out of the palm of the king of Syria and out of the palm of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me.”

9971.label: 2 Kings 16:8
9971.text: Accordingly Aʹhaz took the silver and the gold that was to be found at the house of Jehovah and in the treasures of the king’s house and sent the king of As·syrʹi·a a bribe.

9972.label: 2 Kings 16:9
9972.text: At that the king of As·syrʹi·a listened to him and the king of As·syrʹi·a went up to Damascus and captured it and led its [people] into exile at Kir, and Reʹzin he put to death.

9973.label: 2 Kings 16:10
9973.text: Then King Aʹhaz went to meet Tigʹlath-pil·eʹser the king of As·syrʹi·a at Damascus, and he got to see the altar that was in Damascus. So King Aʹhaz sent U·riʹjah the priest the design of the altar and its pattern as respects all its workmanship.

9974.label: 2 Kings 16:11
9974.text: And U·riʹjah the priest proceeded to build the altar. According to all that King Aʹhaz had sent from Damascus was the way that U·riʹjah the priest made it, pending the time that King Aʹhaz came from Damascus.

9975.label: 2 Kings 16:12
9975.text: When the king came from Damascus, the king got to see the altar; and the king began to go near to the altar and make offerings upon it.

9976.label: 2 Kings 16:13
9976.text: And he continued to make his burnt offering and his grain offering smoke and to pour out his drink offering and to sprinkle the blood of the communion sacrifices that were his upon the altar.

9977.label: 2 Kings 16:14
9977.text: And the copper altar that was before Jehovah he now brought near from in front of the house, from between his altar and the house of Jehovah, and put it at the north side of his altar.

9978.label: 2 Kings 16:15
9978.text: And King Aʹhaz went on to command him, even U·riʹjah the priest, saying: “Upon the great altar make the burnt offering of the morning smoke, also the grain offering of the evening and the burnt offering of the king and his grain offering and the burnt offering of all the people of the land and their grain offering and their drink offerings; and all the blood of burnt offering and all the blood of a sacrifice you should sprinkle upon it. As for the copper altar, it will become something for me to take under consideration.”

9979.label: 2 Kings 16:16
9979.text: And U·riʹjah the priest went doing according to all that King Aʹhaz had commanded.

9980.label: 2 Kings 16:17
9980.text: Furthermore, King Aʹhaz cut the sidewalls of the carriages in pieces and removed from off them the basins; and the sea he took down off the copper bulls that were underneath it and then put it upon a stone pavement.

9981.label: 2 Kings 16:18
9981.text: And the covered structure for the sabbath that they had built in the house and the king’s outer entryway he shifted from the house of Jehovah because of the king of As·syrʹi·a.

9982.label: 2 Kings 16:19
9982.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Aʹhaz, what he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

9983.label: 2 Kings 16:20
9983.text: Finally Aʹhaz lay down with his forefathers and was buried with his forefathers in the City of David; and Hez·e·kiʹah his son began to reign in place of him.

9984.label: 2 Kings 17:1
9984.text: In the twelfth year of Aʹhaz the king of Judah, Ho·sheʹa the son of Eʹlah became king in Sa·marʹi·a over Israel for nine years.

9985.label: 2 Kings 17:2
9985.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, only not as the kings of Israel that happened to be prior to him.

9986.label: 2 Kings 17:3
9986.text: It was against him that Shal·man·eʹser the king of As·syrʹi·a came up, and Ho·sheʹa came to be his servant and began to pay tribute to him.

9987.label: 2 Kings 17:4
9987.text: However, the king of As·syrʹi·a got to find conspiracy in Ho·sheʹa’s case, in that he had sent messengers to So the king of Egypt and did not bring the tribute up to the king of As·syrʹi·a as in former years. Hence the king of As·syrʹi·a shut him up and kept him bound in the house of detention.

9988.label: 2 Kings 17:5
9988.text: And the king of As·syrʹi·a proceeded to come up against all the land and to come up to Sa·marʹi·a and lay siege against it for three years.

9989.label: 2 Kings 17:6
9989.text: In the ninth year of Ho·sheʹa, the king of As·syrʹi·a captured Sa·marʹi·a and then led Israel into exile in As·syrʹi·a and kept them dwelling in Haʹlah and in Haʹbor at the river Goʹzan and in the cities of the Medes.

9990.label: 2 Kings 17:7
9990.text: And it came about because the sons of Israel had sinned against Jehovah their God, who brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt, and they began to fear other gods;

9991.label: 2 Kings 17:8
9991.text: and they kept walking in the statutes of the nations whom Jehovah had driven out from before the sons of Israel, and [in the statutes of] the kings of Israel that they had made;

9992.label: 2 Kings 17:9
9992.text: and the sons of Israel went searching into the things that were not right toward Jehovah their God and kept building themselves high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen clear to the fortified city;

9993.label: 2 Kings 17:10
9993.text: and they kept setting up for themselves sacred pillars and sacred poles upon every high hill and under every luxuriant tree;

9994.label: 2 Kings 17:11
9994.text: and there on all the high places they continued to make sacrificial smoke the same as the nations whom Jehovah had taken into exile because of them, and they kept doing bad things to offend Jehovah;

9995.label: 2 Kings 17:12
9995.text: And they continued to serve dungy idols, concerning which Jehovah had said to them: “YOU must not do this thing”;

9996.label: 2 Kings 17:13
9996.text: and Jehovah kept warning Israel and Judah by means of all his prophets [and] every visionary, saying: “Turn back from YOUR bad ways and keep my commandments, my statutes, according to all the law that I commanded YOUR forefathers and that I have sent to YOU by means of my servants the prophets”;

9997.label: 2 Kings 17:14
9997.text: and they did not listen but kept hardening their necks like the necks of their forefathers that had not exercised faith in Jehovah their God;

9998.label: 2 Kings 17:15
9998.text: and they continued rejecting his regulations and his covenant that he had concluded with their forefathers and his reminders with which he had warned them, and they went following vain idols and became vain themselves, even in imitation of the nations that were all around them, concerning whom Jehovah had commanded them not to do like them;

9999.label: 2 Kings 17:16
9999.text: And they kept leaving all the commandments of Jehovah their God and proceeded to make for themselves molten statues, two calves, and to make a sacred pole, and they began to bow down to all the army of the heavens and to serve Baʹal;

10000.label: 2 Kings 17:17
10000.text: and they continued to make their sons and their daughters pass through the fire and to practice divination and to look for omens, and they kept selling themselves to do what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah, to offend him;

10001.label: 2 Kings 17:18
10001.text: Therefore Jehovah got very incensed against Israel, so that he removed them from his sight. He did not let any remain but the tribe of Judah alone.

10002.label: 2 Kings 17:19
10002.text: Even Judah itself did not keep the commandments of Jehovah their God, but they went walking in the statutes of Israel that they had made.

10003.label: 2 Kings 17:20
10003.text: Consequently Jehovah rejected all the seed of Israel and kept afflicting them and giving them into the hand of pillagers, until he had cast them away from before him.

10004.label: 2 Kings 17:21
10004.text: For he ripped Israel off from the house of David, and they proceeded to make Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat king; and Jer·o·boʹam proceeded to part Israel from following Jehovah, and he caused them to sin with a great sin.

10005.label: 2 Kings 17:22
10005.text: And the sons of Israel went walking in all the sins of Jer·o·boʹam that he had done. They did not depart from them,

10006.label: 2 Kings 17:23
10006.text: until Jehovah removed Israel from his sight, just as he had spoken by means of all his servants the prophets. So Israel went off its own soil into exile in As·syrʹi·a down to this day.

10007.label: 2 Kings 17:24
10007.text: Subsequently the king of As·syrʹi·a brought people from Babylon and Cuʹthah and Avʹva and Haʹmath and Seph·ar·vaʹim and had them dwell in the cities of Sa·marʹi·a instead of the sons of Israel; and they began to take possession of Sa·marʹi·a and to dwell in its cities.

10008.label: 2 Kings 17:25
10008.text: And it came about at the start of their dwelling there that they did not fear Jehovah. Therefore Jehovah sent lions among them, and they came to be killers among them.

10009.label: 2 Kings 17:26
10009.text: So they sent word to the king of As·syrʹi·a, saying: “The nations that you have taken into exile and then settled in the cities of Sa·marʹi·a have not known the religion of the God of the land, so that he keeps sending lions among them; and, look! they are putting them to death, inasmuch as there are none knowing the religion of the God of the land.”

10010.label: 2 Kings 17:27
10010.text: At that the king of As·syrʹi·a commanded, saying: “Have one of the priests go there whom YOU led into exile from there, that he may go and dwell there and teach them the religion of the God of the land.”

10011.label: 2 Kings 17:28
10011.text: Accordingly one of the priests whom they had led into exile from Sa·marʹi·a came and began dwelling in Bethʹel, and he came to be a teacher of them as to how they ought to fear Jehovah.

10012.label: 2 Kings 17:29
10012.text: However, each different nation came to be a maker of its own god, which they then deposited in the house of the high places that the Sa·marʹi·tans had made, each different nation, in their cities where they were dwelling.

10013.label: 2 Kings 17:30
10013.text: And the men of Babylon, for their part, made Sucʹcoth-beʹnoth, and the men of Cuth, for their part, made Nerʹgal, and the men of Haʹmath, for their part, made A·shiʹma.

10014.label: 2 Kings 17:31
10014.text: As for the Avʹvites, they made Nibʹhaz and Tarʹtak; and the Seʹphar·vites were burning their sons in the fire to A·dramʹme·lech and A·namʹme·lech the gods of Seph·ar·vaʹim.

10015.label: 2 Kings 17:32
10015.text: And they came to be fearers of Jehovah and went making for themselves from the people in general priests of high places, and they came to be functionaries for them in the house of the high places.

10016.label: 2 Kings 17:33
10016.text: It was of Jehovah that they became fearers, but it was of their own gods that they proved to be worshipers, according to the religion of the nations from among whom they had led them into exile.

10017.label: 2 Kings 17:34
10017.text: Down to this day they are doing according to their former religions. There were none fearing Jehovah and none doing according to his statutes and his judicial decisions and the law and the commandment that Jehovah had commanded the sons of Jacob, whose name he made Israel;

10018.label: 2 Kings 17:35
10018.text: when Jehovah concluded a covenant with them and commanded them, saying: “YOU must not fear other gods, and YOU must not bow down to them nor serve them nor sacrifice to them.

10019.label: 2 Kings 17:36
10019.text: But Jehovah, who brought YOU up out of the land of Egypt with great power and a stretched-out arm, is the One whom YOU should fear, and to him YOU should bow down, and to him YOU should sacrifice.

10020.label: 2 Kings 17:37
10020.text: And the regulations and the judicial decisions and the law and the commandment that he wrote for YOU, YOU should take care to do always; and YOU must not fear other gods.

10021.label: 2 Kings 17:38
10021.text: And the covenant that I have concluded with YOU, YOU must not forget; and YOU must not fear other gods.

10022.label: 2 Kings 17:39
10022.text: But it is Jehovah YOUR God that YOU should fear, as he is the one that will deliver YOU out of the hand of all YOUR enemies.”

10023.label: 2 Kings 17:40
10023.text: And they did not obey, but it was according to their former religion that they were doing.

10024.label: 2 Kings 17:41
10024.text: And these nations came to be fearers of Jehovah, but it was their own graven images that they proved to be serving. As for both their sons and their grandsons, it was just as their forefathers had done that they themselves are doing down to this day.

10025.label: 2 Kings 18:1
10025.text: And it came about in the third year of Ho·sheʹa the son of Eʹlah the king of Israel that Hez·e·kiʹah the son of Aʹhaz the king of Judah became king.

10026.label: 2 Kings 18:2
10026.text: Twenty-five years old he happened to be when he began to reign, and for twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Aʹbi the daughter of Zech·a·riʹah.

10027.label: 2 Kings 18:3
10027.text: And he continued to do what was right in Jehovah’s eyes, according to all that David his forefather had done.

10028.label: 2 Kings 18:4
10028.text: He it was that removed the high places and broke the sacred pillars to pieces and cut down the sacred pole and crushed to pieces the copper serpent that Moses had made; for down to those days the sons of Israel had continually been making sacrificial smoke to it, and it used to be called the copper serpent-idol.

10029.label: 2 Kings 18:5
10029.text: In Jehovah the God of Israel he trusted; and after him there proved to be no one like him among all the kings of Judah, even those who had happened to be prior to him.

10030.label: 2 Kings 18:6
10030.text: And he kept sticking to Jehovah. He did not turn aside from following him, but he continued keeping his commandments that Jehovah had commanded Moses.

10031.label: 2 Kings 18:7
10031.text: And Jehovah proved to be with him. Wherever he would go out, he would act prudently; and he proceeded to rebel against the king of As·syrʹi·a and did not serve him.

10032.label: 2 Kings 18:8
10032.text: It was he that struck down the Phi·lisʹtines clear to Gaʹza and also its territories, from the tower of the watchmen clear to the fortified city.

10033.label: 2 Kings 18:9
10033.text: And it came about in the fourth year of King Hez·e·kiʹah, that is, the seventh year of Ho·sheʹa the son of Eʹlah the king of Israel, that Shal·man·eʹser the king of As·syrʹi·a came up against Sa·marʹi·a and began to lay siege to it.

10034.label: 2 Kings 18:10
10034.text: And they got to capture it at the end of three years; in the sixth year of Hez·e·kiʹah, that is, the ninth year of Ho·sheʹa the king of Israel, Sa·marʹi·a was captured.

10035.label: 2 Kings 18:11
10035.text: After that the king of As·syrʹi·a took Israel into exile in As·syrʹi·a and set them down in Haʹlah and in Haʹbor at the river Goʹzan and in the cities of the Medes,

10036.label: 2 Kings 18:12
10036.text: over the fact that they had not listened to the voice of Jehovah their God, but kept overstepping his covenant, even all that Moses the servant of Jehovah had commanded. They neither listened nor performed.

10037.label: 2 Kings 18:13
10037.text: And in the fourteenth year of King Hez·e·kiʹah, Sen·nachʹer·ib the king of As·syrʹi·a came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and proceeded to seize them.

10038.label: 2 Kings 18:14
10038.text: So Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah sent to the king of As·syrʹi·a at Laʹchish, saying: “I have sinned. Turn back from against me. Whatever you may impose upon me I shall carry.” Accordingly the king of As·syrʹi·a laid upon Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah three hundred silver talents and thirty gold talents.

10039.label: 2 Kings 18:15
10039.text: Therefore Hez·e·kiʹah gave all the silver that was to be found at the house of Jehovah and in the treasures of the king’s house.

10040.label: 2 Kings 18:16
10040.text: At that time Hez·e·kiʹah cut off the doors of the temple of Jehovah and the doorposts that Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah had overlaid and then gave them to the king of As·syrʹi·a.

10041.label: 2 Kings 18:17
10041.text: And the king of As·syrʹi·a proceeded to send Tarʹtan and Rabʹsa·ris and Rabʹsha·keh from Laʹchish to King Hez·e·kiʹah with a heavy military force to Jerusalem, that they might go up and come to Jerusalem. So they went up and came and stood still by the conduit of the upper pool, which is at the highway of the laundryman’s field.

10042.label: 2 Kings 18:18
10042.text: And they began to call out to the king, but there came out to them E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah, who was over the household, and Shebʹnah the secretary and Joʹah the son of Aʹsaph the recorder.

10043.label: 2 Kings 18:19
10043.text: Accordingly Rabʹsha·keh said to them: “Please, say to Hez·e·kiʹah, ‘This is what the great king, the king of As·syrʹi·a, has said: “What is this confidence in which you have trusted?

10044.label: 2 Kings 18:20
10044.text: You have said (but it is the word of lips), ‘There are counsel and mightiness for the war.’ Now in whom have you put your trust, that you have rebelled against me?

10045.label: 2 Kings 18:21
10045.text: Now, look! you have put your trust in the support of this crushed reed, Egypt, which, if a man should brace himself upon it, would certainly enter into his palm and pierce it. That is the way Pharʹaoh the king of Egypt is to all those putting their trust in him.

10046.label: 2 Kings 18:22
10046.text: And in case YOU men should say to me, ‘It is Jehovah our God in whom we have put our trust,’ is he not the one whose high places and whose altars Hez·e·kiʹah has removed, while he says to Judah and Jerusalem, ‘Before this altar YOU should bow down in Jerusalem’?”’

10047.label: 2 Kings 18:23
10047.text: Now, then, make a wager, please, with my lord the king of As·syrʹi·a, and let me give you two thousand horses [to see] whether you are able, on your part, to put riders upon them.

10048.label: 2 Kings 18:24
10048.text: How, then, could you turn back the face of one governor of the smallest servants of my lord, while you, for your part, put your trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

10049.label: 2 Kings 18:25
10049.text: Now is it without authorization from Jehovah that I have come up against this place to bring it to ruin? Jehovah himself said to me, ‘Go up against this land, and you must bring it to ruin.’”

10050.label: 2 Kings 18:26
10050.text: At this E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah and Shebʹnah and Joʹah said to Rabʹsha·keh: “Speak with your servants, please, in the Syrian language, for we can listen; and do not speak with us in the Jews’ language in the ears of the people that are on the wall.”

10051.label: 2 Kings 18:27
10051.text: But Rabʹsha·keh said to them: “Is it to your lord and to you that my lord has sent me to speak these words? Is it not to the men sitting upon the wall, that they may eat their own excrement and drink their own urine with YOU men?”

10052.label: 2 Kings 18:28
10052.text: And Rabʹsha·keh continued to stand and call out in a loud voice in the Jews’ language; and he went on to speak and say: “HEAR the word of the great king, the king of As·syrʹi·a.

10053.label: 2 Kings 18:29
10053.text: This is what the king has said, ‘Do not let Hez·e·kiʹah deceive YOU people, for he is not able to deliver YOU out of my hand.

10054.label: 2 Kings 18:30
10054.text: And do not let Hez·e·kiʹah cause YOU to trust in Jehovah, saying: “Without fail Jehovah will deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a.”

10055.label: 2 Kings 18:31
10055.text: Do not listen to Hez·e·kiʹah; for this is what the king of As·syrʹi·a has said: “Make a capitulation to me, and come out to me, and eat each one from his own vine and each one from his own fig tree and drink each one the water of his own cistern,

10056.label: 2 Kings 18:32
10056.text: until I come and I actually take YOU to a land like YOUR own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of oil-olive trees and honey; and keep living that YOU may not die. And do not listen to Hez·e·kiʹah, for he allures YOU, saying, ‘Jehovah himself will deliver us.’

10057.label: 2 Kings 18:33
10057.text: Have the gods of the nations at all delivered each one his own land out of the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a?

10058.label: 2 Kings 18:34
10058.text: Where are the gods of Haʹmath and Arʹpad? Where are the gods of Seph·ar·vaʹim, Heʹna and Ivʹvah? Have they delivered Sa·marʹi·a out of my hand?

10059.label: 2 Kings 18:35
10059.text: Who are there among all the gods of the lands that have delivered their land out of my hand, so that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?”’”

10060.label: 2 Kings 18:36
10060.text: And the people kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the commandment of the king was, saying: “YOU must not answer him.”

10061.label: 2 Kings 18:37
10061.text: But E·liʹa·kim the son of Hil·kiʹah, who was over the household, and Shebʹnah the secretary and Joʹah the son of Aʹsaph the recorder came to Hez·e·kiʹah with their garments ripped apart and told him the words of Rabʹsha·keh.

10062.label: 2 Kings 19:1
10062.text: And it came about that as soon as King Hez·e·kiʹah heard, he immediately ripped his garments apart and covered himself with sackcloth and came into the house of Jehovah.

10063.label: 2 Kings 19:2
10063.text: Further, he sent E·liʹa·kim, who was over the household, and Shebʹnah the secretary and the older men of the priests covered with sackcloth to Isaiah the prophet the son of Aʹmoz.

10064.label: 2 Kings 19:3
10064.text: And they proceeded to say to him: “This is what Hez·e·kiʹah has said, ‘This day is a day of distress and of rebuke and of scornful insolence; for the sons have come as far as the womb’s mouth, and there is no power to give birth.

10065.label: 2 Kings 19:4
10065.text: Perhaps Jehovah your God will hear all the words of Rabʹsha·keh, whom the king of As·syrʹi·a his lord sent to taunt the living God, and he will actually call him to account for the words that Jehovah your God has heard. And you must lift up prayer in behalf of the remnant that are to be found.’”

10066.label: 2 Kings 19:5
10066.text: So the servants of King Hez·e·kiʹah came in to Isaiah.

10067.label: 2 Kings 19:6
10067.text: Then Isaiah said to them: “This is what YOU should say to YOUR lord, ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard with which the attendants of the king of As·syrʹi·a spoke abusively of me.

10068.label: 2 Kings 19:7
10068.text: Here I am putting a spirit in him, and he must hear a report and return to his own land; and I shall certainly cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”

10069.label: 2 Kings 19:8
10069.text: After that Rabʹsha·keh returned and found the king of As·syrʹi·a fighting against Libʹnah; for he had heard that he had pulled away from Laʹchish.

10070.label: 2 Kings 19:9
10070.text: He heard it said respecting Tir·haʹkah the king of E·thi·oʹpi·a: “Here he has come out to fight against you.” Therefore he sent messengers again to Hez·e·kiʹah, saying:

10071.label: 2 Kings 19:10
10071.text: “This is what YOU men should say to Hez·e·kiʹah the king of Judah, ‘Do not let your God in whom you are trusting deceive you, saying: “Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of As·syrʹi·a.”

10072.label: 2 Kings 19:11
10072.text: Look! You yourself have heard what the kings of As·syrʹi·a did to all the lands by devoting them to destruction; and will you yourself be delivered?

10073.label: 2 Kings 19:12
10073.text: Have the gods of the nations that my forefathers brought to ruin delivered them, even Goʹzan and Haʹran and Reʹzeph and the sons of Eʹden that were in Tel-asʹsar?

10074.label: 2 Kings 19:13
10074.text: Where is he—the king of Haʹmath and the king of Arʹpad and the king of the cities of Seph·ar·vaʹim, Heʹna and Ivʹvah?’”

10075.label: 2 Kings 19:14
10075.text: Then Hez·e·kiʹah took the letters out of the hand of the messengers and read them, after which Hez·e·kiʹah went up to the house of Jehovah and spread it out before Jehovah.

10076.label: 2 Kings 19:15
10076.text: And Hez·e·kiʹah began to pray before Jehovah and say: “O Jehovah the God of Israel, sitting upon the cherubs, you alone are the [true] God of all the kingdoms of the earth. You yourself have made the heavens and the earth.

10077.label: 2 Kings 19:16
10077.text: Incline your ear, O Jehovah, and hear. Open your eyes, O Jehovah, and see, and hear the words of Sen·nachʹer·ib that he has sent to taunt the living God.

10078.label: 2 Kings 19:17
10078.text: It is a fact, O Jehovah, the kings of As·syrʹi·a have devastated the nations and their land.

10079.label: 2 Kings 19:18
10079.text: And they have consigned their gods to the fire, because they were no gods, but the workmanship of man’s hands, wood and stone; so that they destroyed them.

10080.label: 2 Kings 19:19
10080.text: And now, O Jehovah our God, save us, please, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, O Jehovah, are God alone.”

10081.label: 2 Kings 19:20
10081.text: And Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz proceeded to send to Hez·e·kiʹah, saying: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘The prayer that you have made to me concerning Sen·nachʹer·ib the king of As·syrʹi·a I have heard.

10082.label: 2 Kings 19:21
10082.text: This is the word that Jehovah has spoken against him: “The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you, she has held you in derision. Behind you the daughter of Jerusalem has wagged her head.

10083.label: 2 Kings 19:22
10083.text: Whom have you taunted and spoken of abusively? And against whom have you lifted up your voice And do you raise your eyes on high? It is against the Holy One of Israel!

10084.label: 2 Kings 19:23
10084.text: By means of your messengers you have taunted Jehovah and you say, ‘With the multitude of my war chariots I myself —I shall certainly ascend the height of mountainous regions, The remotest parts of Lebʹa·non; And I shall cut down its lofty cedars, its choice juniper trees. And I will enter its final lodging place, the forest of its orchard.

10085.label: 2 Kings 19:24
10085.text: I myself shall certainly dig and drink strange waters,And I shall dry up with the soles of my feet all the Nile canals of Egypt.’

10086.label: 2 Kings 19:25
10086.text: Have you not heard? From remote times it is what I will do. From bygone days I have even formed it. Now I will bring it in. And you will serve to make fortified cities desolate as piles of ruins.

10087.label: 2 Kings 19:26
10087.text: And their inhabitants will be feeble-handed; They will simply be terrified and will be ashamed. They must become as vegetation of the field and green tender grass, Grass of the roofs, when there is a scorching before the east wind.

10088.label: 2 Kings 19:27
10088.text: And your sitting quiet and your going out and your coming in I well know, And your exciting yourself against me,

10089.label: 2 Kings 19:28
10089.text: Because your exciting yourself against me and your roaring have come up into my ears. And I shall certainly put my hook in your nose and my bridle between your lips, And I shall indeed lead you back by the way by which you have come.”

10090.label: 2 Kings 19:29
10090.text: “‘And this will be the sign for you: There will be an eating this year of the growth from spilled kernels, and in the second year grain that shoots up of itself; but in the third year sow seed, you people, and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruitage.

10091.label: 2 Kings 19:30
10091.text: And those who escape of the house of Judah, those who are left, will certainly take root downward and produce fruitage upward.

10092.label: 2 Kings 19:31
10092.text: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and those who escape from Mount Zion. The very zeal of Jehovah of armies will do this.

10093.label: 2 Kings 19:32
10093.text: “‘That is why this is what Jehovah has said concerning the king of As·syrʹi·a: “He will not come into this city nor will he shoot an arrow there nor confront it with a shield nor cast up a siege rampart against it.

10094.label: 2 Kings 19:33
10094.text: By the way by which he proceeded to come, he will return, and into this city he will not come, is the utterance of Jehovah.

10095.label: 2 Kings 19:34
10095.text: And I shall certainly defend this city to save it for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.”’”

10096.label: 2 Kings 19:35
10096.text: And it came about on that night that the angel of Jehovah proceeded to go out and strike down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the As·syrʹi·ans. When people rose up early in the morning, why, there all of them were dead carcasses.

10097.label: 2 Kings 19:36
10097.text: Therefore Sen·nachʹer·ib the king of As·syrʹi·a pulled away and went and returned, and he took up dwelling in Ninʹe·veh.

10098.label: 2 Kings 19:37
10098.text: And it came about that as he was bowing down at the house of Nisʹroch his god, A·dramʹme·lech and Shar·eʹzer, his sons, themselves struck him down with the sword, and they themselves escaped to the land of Arʹa·rat. And Eʹsar-hadʹdon his son began to reign in place of him.

10099.label: 2 Kings 20:1
10099.text: In those days Hez·e·kiʹah got sick to the point of dying. Accordingly Isaiah the son of Aʹmoz the prophet came in to him and said to him: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘Give commands to your household, for you yourself will indeed die and will not live.’”

10100.label: 2 Kings 20:2
10100.text: At that he turned his face to the wall and began to pray to Jehovah, saying:

10101.label: 2 Kings 20:3
10101.text: “I beseech you, O Jehovah, remember, please, how I have walked before you in truthfulness and with a complete heart, and what was good in your eyes I have done.” And Hez·e·kiʹah began to weep profusely.

10102.label: 2 Kings 20:4
10102.text: And it came about that Isaiah himself had not yet gone out to the middle court when Jehovah’s word itself came to him, saying:

10103.label: 2 Kings 20:5
10103.text: “Go back, and you must say to Hez·e·kiʹah the leader of my people, ‘This is what Jehovah the God of David your forefather has said: “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Here I am healing you. On the third day you will go up to the house of Jehovah.

10104.label: 2 Kings 20:6
10104.text: And I shall certainly add fifteen years to your days, and out of the palm of the king of As·syrʹi·a I shall deliver you and this city, and I will defend this city for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.”’”

10105.label: 2 Kings 20:7
10105.text: And Isaiah went on to say: “YOU men, take a cake of pressed dried figs.” So they took and put it upon the boil, after which he gradually revived.

10106.label: 2 Kings 20:8
10106.text: Meantime, Hez·e·kiʹah said to Isaiah: “What is the sign that Jehovah will heal me and I shall certainly go up on the third day to the house of Jehovah?”

10107.label: 2 Kings 20:9
10107.text: To this Isaiah said: “This is the sign for you from Jehovah that Jehovah will perform the word that he has spoken: Shall the shadow actually go forward ten steps [of the stairs] or should it go back ten steps?”

10108.label: 2 Kings 20:10
10108.text: Then Hez·e·kiʹah said: “It is an easy thing for the shadow to extend itself ten steps, but not that the shadow should go backward ten steps.”

10109.label: 2 Kings 20:11
10109.text: At that Isaiah the prophet began to call out to Jehovah; and he made the shadow that had gone down gradually go back on the steps, that is, on the steps [of the stairs] of Aʹhaz, ten steps backward.

10110.label: 2 Kings 20:12
10110.text: At that time Be·roʹdach-balʹa·dan the son of Balʹa·dan the king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hez·e·kiʹah; for he had heard that Hez·e·kiʹah had been sick.

10111.label: 2 Kings 20:13
10111.text: And Hez·e·kiʹah proceeded to listen to them and show them all his treasure-house, the silver and the gold and the balsam oil and the good oil and his armory and all that was to be found in his treasures. There proved to be nothing that Hez·e·kiʹah did not show them in his own house and in all his dominion.

10112.label: 2 Kings 20:14
10112.text: After that Isaiah the prophet came in to King Hez·e·kiʹah and said to him: “What did these men say and from where did they proceed to come to you?” So Hez·e·kiʹah said: “From a distant land they came, from Babylon.”

10113.label: 2 Kings 20:15
10113.text: And he went on to say: “What did they see in your house?” To this Hez·e·kiʹah said: “Everything that is in my house they saw. There proved to be nothing that I did not show them in my treasures.”

10114.label: 2 Kings 20:16
10114.text: Isaiah now said to Hez·e·kiʹah: “Hear the word of Jehovah,

10115.label: 2 Kings 20:17
10115.text: ‘“Look! Days are coming, and all that is in your own house and that your forefathers have stored up down to this day will actually be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,” Jehovah has said.

10116.label: 2 Kings 20:18
10116.text: “And some of your own sons that will come forth from you to whom you will become father will themselves be taken and actually become court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.”’”

10117.label: 2 Kings 20:19
10117.text: At that Hez·e·kiʹah said to Isaiah: “The word of Jehovah that you have spoken is good.” And he went on to say: “Is it not so, if peace and truth themselves will continue in my own days?”

10118.label: 2 Kings 20:20
10118.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Hez·e·kiʹah and all his mightiness and how he made the pool and the conduit and then brought the water into the city, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

10119.label: 2 Kings 20:21
10119.text: Finally Hez·e·kiʹah lay down with his forefathers; and Ma·nasʹseh his son began to reign in place of him.

10120.label: 2 Kings 21:1
10120.text: Twelve years old was Ma·nasʹseh when he began to reign, and for fifty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Hephʹzi·bah.

10121.label: 2 Kings 21:2
10121.text: And he proceeded to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, according to the detestable things of the nations that Jehovah had driven out from before the sons of Israel.

10122.label: 2 Kings 21:3
10122.text: So he built again the high places that Hez·e·kiʹah his father had destroyed, and set up altars to Baʹal and made a sacred pole, just as Aʹhab the king of Israel had done; and he began to bow down to all the army of the heavens and to serve them.

10123.label: 2 Kings 21:4
10123.text: And he built altars in the house of Jehovah, respecting which Jehovah had said: “In Jerusalem I shall put my name.”

10124.label: 2 Kings 21:5
10124.text: And he went on to build altars to all the army of the heavens in two courtyards of the house of Jehovah.

10125.label: 2 Kings 21:6
10125.text: And he made his own son pass through the fire, and he practiced magic and looked for omens and made spirit mediums and professional foretellers of events. He did on a large scale what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, to offend him.

10126.label: 2 Kings 21:7
10126.text: Further, he put the carved image of the sacred pole that he had made in the house of which Jehovah had said to David and to Solʹo·mon his son: “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I shall put my name to time indefinite.

10127.label: 2 Kings 21:8
10127.text: And I shall not again make the foot of Israel wander from the ground that I gave to their forefathers, provided only they are careful to do according to all that I have commanded them, even concerning all the law that my servant Moses commanded them.”

10128.label: 2 Kings 21:9
10128.text: And they did not listen, but Ma·nasʹseh kept seducing them to do what was bad more than the nations whom Jehovah had annihilated from before the sons of Israel.

10129.label: 2 Kings 21:10
10129.text: And Jehovah kept speaking by means of his servants the prophets, saying:

10130.label: 2 Kings 21:11
10130.text: “For the reason that Ma·nasʹseh the king of Judah has done these detestable things, he has acted more wickedly than all that the Amʹor·ites did that were prior to him, and he proceeded to make even Judah sin with his dungy idols.

10131.label: 2 Kings 21:12
10131.text: That is why this is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘Here I am bringing a calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah, of which if anyone hears both his ears will tingle.

10132.label: 2 Kings 21:13
10132.text: And I shall certainly stretch upon Jerusalem the measuring line applied to Sa·marʹi·a and also the leveling instrument applied to the house of Aʹhab; and I shall simply wipe Jerusalem clean just as one wipes the handleless bowl clean, wiping it clean and turning it upside down.

10133.label: 2 Kings 21:14
10133.text: And I shall indeed forsake the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hand of their enemies, and they will simply become plunder and pillage to all their enemies,

10134.label: 2 Kings 21:15
10134.text: for the reason that they did what was bad in my eyes and were continually offending me from the day that their forefathers came out from Egypt down to this day.’”

10135.label: 2 Kings 21:16
10135.text: And there was also innocent blood that Ma·nasʹseh shed in very great quantity, until he had filled Jerusalem from end to end, besides his sin with which he caused Judah to sin by doing what was bad in the eyes of Jehovah.

10136.label: 2 Kings 21:17
10136.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Ma·nasʹseh and all that he did and his sin with which he sinned, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

10137.label: 2 Kings 21:18
10137.text: Finally Ma·nasʹseh lay down with his forefathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzʹza; and Aʹmon his son began to reign in place of him.

10138.label: 2 Kings 21:19
10138.text: Twenty-two years old was Aʹmon when he began to reign, and for two years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Me·shulʹle·meth the daughter of Haʹruz from Jotʹbah.

10139.label: 2 Kings 21:20
10139.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, just as Ma·nasʹseh his father had done.

10140.label: 2 Kings 21:21
10140.text: And he kept walking in all the way that his father had walked, and he continued serving the dungy idols that his father had served and bowing down to them.

10141.label: 2 Kings 21:22
10141.text: Thus he left Jehovah the God of his forefathers, and he did not walk in the way of Jehovah.

10142.label: 2 Kings 21:23
10142.text: Eventually servants of Aʹmon conspired against him and put the king to death in his own house.

10143.label: 2 Kings 21:24
10143.text: But the people of the land struck down all the conspirators against King Aʹmon. Then the people of the land made Jo·siʹah his son king in place of him.

10144.label: 2 Kings 21:25
10144.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Aʹmon, what he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

10145.label: 2 Kings 21:26
10145.text: So they buried him in his grave in the garden of Uzʹza; and Jo·siʹah his son began to reign in place of him.

10146.label: 2 Kings 22:1
10146.text: Eight years old was Jo·siʹah when he began to reign, and for thirty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Je·diʹdah the daughter of A·daiʹah from Bozʹkath.

10147.label: 2 Kings 22:2
10147.text: And he proceeded to do what was right in Jehovah’s eyes and to walk in all the way of David his forefather, and he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

10148.label: 2 Kings 22:3
10148.text: And it came about in the eighteenth year of King Jo·siʹah that the king sent Shaʹphan the son of Az·a·liʹah the son of Me·shulʹlam the secretary to the house of Jehovah, saying:

10149.label: 2 Kings 22:4
10149.text: “Go up to Hil·kiʹah the high priest, and let him complete the money that is being brought into the house of Jehovah that the doorkeepers have gathered from the people;

10150.label: 2 Kings 22:5
10150.text: and let them put it into the hand of those doing the work, the appointed ones, in the house of Jehovah, that they may give it to those doing the work who are in the house of Jehovah to repair the cracks of the house,

10151.label: 2 Kings 22:6
10151.text: to the craftsmen and the builders and the masons, and to buy timbers and hewn stones to repair the house.

10152.label: 2 Kings 22:7
10152.text: Only no accounting should be taken of the money with them into whose hand it is being put, for it is in faithfulness that they are working.”

10153.label: 2 Kings 22:8
10153.text: Later Hil·kiʹah the high priest said to Shaʹphan the secretary: “The very book of the law I have found in the house of Jehovah.” So Hil·kiʹah gave the book to Shaʹphan, and he began to read it.

10154.label: 2 Kings 22:9
10154.text: Then Shaʹphan the secretary came in to the king and replied to the king and said: “Your servants have poured out the money that was to be found in the house, and they keep putting it into the hand of the doers of the work, the ones appointed, in the house of Jehovah.”

10155.label: 2 Kings 22:10
10155.text: And Shaʹphan the secretary went on to tell the king, saying: “There is a book that Hil·kiʹah the priest has given me.” And Shaʹphan began to read it before the king.

10156.label: 2 Kings 22:11
10156.text: And it came about that as soon as the king heard the words of the book of the law, he immediately ripped his garments apart.

10157.label: 2 Kings 22:12
10157.text: Then the king commanded Hil·kiʹah the priest and A·hiʹkam the son of Shaʹphan and Achʹbor the son of Mi·caiʹah and Shaʹphan the secretary and A·saiʹah the king’s servant, saying:

10158.label: 2 Kings 22:13
10158.text: “Go, inquire of Jehovah in my own behalf and in behalf of the people and in behalf of all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is Jehovah’s rage that has been set afire against us over the fact that our forefathers did not listen to the words of this book by doing according to all that is written concerning us.”

10159.label: 2 Kings 22:14
10159.text: Accordingly Hil·kiʹah the priest and A·hiʹkam and Achʹbor and Shaʹphan and A·saiʹah went to Hulʹdah the prophetess the wife of Shalʹlum the son of Tikʹvah the son of Harʹhas, the caretaker of the garments, as she was dwelling in Jerusalem in the second quarter; and they proceeded to speak to her.

10160.label: 2 Kings 22:15
10160.text: In turn she said to them: “This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said, ‘Say to the man that has sent YOU men to me:

10161.label: 2 Kings 22:16
10161.text: “This is what Jehovah has said, ‘Here I am bringing calamity upon this place and upon its inhabitants, even all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read;

10162.label: 2 Kings 22:17
10162.text: due to the fact that they have left me and have gone making sacrificial smoke to other gods in order to offend me with all the work of their hands, and my rage has been set afire against this place and will not be extinguished.’”’

10163.label: 2 Kings 22:18
10163.text: And as to the king of Judah who is sending YOU to inquire of Jehovah, this is what YOU should say to him, ‘This is what Jehovah the God of Israel has said: “As regards the words that you have heard,

10164.label: 2 Kings 22:19
10164.text: for the reason that your heart was soft so that you humbled yourself because of Jehovah at your hearing what I have spoken against this place and its inhabitants [for it] to become an object of astonishment and a malediction, and then you ripped your garments apart and began weeping before me, I, even I, have heard,” is the utterance of Jehovah.

10165.label: 2 Kings 22:20
10165.text: “That is why here I am gathering you to your forefathers, and you will certainly be gathered to your own graveyard in peace, and your eyes will not look upon all the calamity that I am bringing upon this place.”’” And they proceeded to bring the king the reply.

10166.label: 2 Kings 23:1
10166.text: Then the king sent and they gathered together to him all the older men of Judah and Jerusalem.

10167.label: 2 Kings 23:2
10167.text: After that the king went up to the house of Jehovah, and also all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and also the priests and the prophets and all the people, from small to great; and he began to read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of Jehovah.

10168.label: 2 Kings 23:3
10168.text: And the king kept standing by the pillar and now concluded the covenant before Jehovah, to walk after Jehovah and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all the heart and with all the soul by carrying out the words of this covenant that were written in this book. Accordingly all the people took their stand in the covenant.

10169.label: 2 Kings 23:4
10169.text: And the king went on to command Hil·kiʹah the high priest and the priests of the second rank and the doorkeepers to bring out from the temple of Jehovah all the utensils made for Baʹal and for the sacred pole and for all the army of the heavens. Then he burned them outside Jerusalem on the terraces of Kidʹron, and he brought the dust of them to Bethʹel.

10170.label: 2 Kings 23:5
10170.text: And he put out of business the foreign-god priests, whom the kings of Judah had put in that they might make sacrificial smoke on the high places in the cities of Judah and the surroundings of Jerusalem, and also those making sacrificial smoke to Baʹal, to the sun and to the moon and to the constellations of the zodiac and to all the army of the heavens.

10171.label: 2 Kings 23:6
10171.text: Furthermore, he brought out the sacred pole from the house of Jehovah to the outskirts of Jerusalem, to the torrent valley of Kidʹron, and burned it in the torrent valley of Kidʹron and ground it to dust and cast its dust upon the burial place of the sons of the people.

10172.label: 2 Kings 23:7
10172.text: Further, he pulled down the houses of the male temple prostitutes that were in the house of Jehovah, where the women were weaving tent shrines for the sacred pole.

10173.label: 2 Kings 23:8
10173.text: Then he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah, that he might make unfit for worship the high places where the priests had made sacrificial smoke, from Geʹba as far as Beʹer-sheʹba; and he pulled down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the chief of the city, which was at the left as a person came into the gate of the city.

10174.label: 2 Kings 23:9
10174.text: Only the priests of the high places would not come up to the altar of Jehovah in Jerusalem, but they ate unfermented cakes in among their brothers.

10175.label: 2 Kings 23:10
10175.text: And he made unfit for worship Toʹpheth, which is in the valley of the sons of Hinʹnom, that no one might make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Moʹlech.

10176.label: 2 Kings 23:11
10176.text: Further, he caused the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun to cease from entering the house of Jehovah by the dining room of Naʹthan-melʹech the court official, which was in the porticoes; and the chariots of the sun he burned in the fire.

10177.label: 2 Kings 23:12
10177.text: And the altars that were upon the roof of the roof chamber of Aʹhaz that the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Ma·nasʹseh had made in two courtyards of the house of Jehovah, the king pulled down, after which he crushed them there, and he cast their dust into the torrent valley of Kidʹron.

10178.label: 2 Kings 23:13
10178.text: And the high places that were in front of Jerusalem, that were to the right of the Mount of Ruination, that Solʹo·mon the king of Israel had built to Ashʹto·reth the disgusting thing of the Si·doʹni·ans and to Cheʹmosh the disgusting thing of Moʹab and to Milʹcom the detestable thing of the sons of Amʹmon, the king made unfit for worship.

10179.label: 2 Kings 23:14
10179.text: And he broke the sacred pillars to pieces and went on to cut down the sacred poles and to fill their places with human bones.

10180.label: 2 Kings 23:15
10180.text: And also the altar that was in Bethʹel, the high place that Jer·o·boʹam the son of Neʹbat, who caused Israel to sin, had made, even that altar and the high place he pulled down. Then he burned the high place; he ground [it] to dust and burned the sacred pole.

10181.label: 2 Kings 23:16
10181.text: When Jo·siʹah turned, he got to see the burial places that were there in the mountain. So he sent and took the bones from the burial places and burned them upon the altar, that he might make it unfit for worship, according to Jehovah’s word that the man of the [true] God had proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.

10182.label: 2 Kings 23:17
10182.text: Then he said: “What is the gravestone over there that I am seeing?” At this the men of the city said to him: “It is the burial place of the man of the [true] God that came from Judah and proceeded to proclaim these things that you have done against the altar of Bethʹel.”

10183.label: 2 Kings 23:18
10183.text: So he said: “Let him rest. Do not let anyone disturb his bones.” Consequently they let his bones alone along with the bones of the prophet that had come from Sa·marʹi·a.

10184.label: 2 Kings 23:19
10184.text: And also all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Sa·marʹi·a that the kings of Israel had built to cause offense Jo·siʹah removed, and he went on to do to them according to all the doings that he had done at Bethʹel.

10185.label: 2 Kings 23:20
10185.text: Accordingly he sacrificed all the priests of the high places that were there upon the altars and burned human bones upon them. After that he returned to Jerusalem.

10186.label: 2 Kings 23:21
10186.text: The king now commanded all the people, saying: “Hold a passover to Jehovah YOUR God according to what is written in this book of the covenant.”

10187.label: 2 Kings 23:22
10187.text: For no passover like this had been held from the days of the judges that had judged Israel, nor all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.

10188.label: 2 Kings 23:23
10188.text: But in the eighteenth year of King Jo·siʹah this passover was held to Jehovah in Jerusalem.

10189.label: 2 Kings 23:24
10189.text: And also the spirit mediums and the professional foretellers of events and the teraphim and the dungy idols and all the disgusting things that had appeared in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem Jo·siʹah cleared out, in order that he might actually carry out the words of the law that were written in the book that Hil·kiʹah the priest had found at the house of Jehovah.

10190.label: 2 Kings 23:25
10190.text: And like him there did not prove to be a king prior to him who returned to Jehovah with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his vital force, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him has there risen up one like him.

10191.label: 2 Kings 23:26
10191.text: Nevertheless, Jehovah did not turn back from the great burning of his anger, with which his anger burned against Judah over all the offensive things with which Ma·nasʹseh had made them offend.

10192.label: 2 Kings 23:27
10192.text: But Jehovah said: “Judah, too, I shall remove from my sight, just as I have removed Israel; and I shall certainly reject this city that I have chosen, even Jerusalem, and the house of which I have said, ‘My name will continue there.’”

10193.label: 2 Kings 23:28
10193.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Jo·siʹah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

10194.label: 2 Kings 23:29
10194.text: In his days Pharʹaoh Neʹchoh the king of Egypt came up to the king of As·syrʹi·a by the river Eu·phraʹtes, and King Jo·siʹah proceeded to go to meet him; but he put him to death at Me·gidʹdo as soon as he saw him.

10195.label: 2 Kings 23:30
10195.text: So his servants conveyed him dead in a chariot from Me·gidʹdo and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his grave. Then the people of the land took Je·hoʹa·haz the son of Jo·siʹah and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.

10196.label: 2 Kings 23:31
10196.text: Twenty-three years old was Je·hoʹa·haz when he began to reign, and for three months he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Ha·muʹtal the daughter of Jeremiah from Libʹnah.

10197.label: 2 Kings 23:32
10197.text: And he began to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, according to all that forefathers of his had done.

10198.label: 2 Kings 23:33
10198.text: And Pharʹaoh Neʹchoh got to put him in bonds at Ribʹlah in the land of Haʹmath, to keep him from reigning in Jerusalem, and then imposed a fine upon the land of a hundred silver talents and a gold talent.

10199.label: 2 Kings 23:34
10199.text: Furthermore, Pharʹaoh Neʹchoh made E·liʹa·kim the son of Jo·siʹah king in place of Jo·siʹah his father and changed his name to Je·hoiʹa·kim; and Je·hoʹa·haz he took and then brought to Egypt, where he eventually died.

10200.label: 2 Kings 23:35
10200.text: And the silver and the gold Je·hoiʹa·kim gave to Pharʹaoh. Only he taxed the land, to give the silver at the order of Pharʹaoh. According to each one’s individual tax rate he exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, to give it to Pharʹaoh Neʹchoh.

10201.label: 2 Kings 23:36
10201.text: Twenty-five years old was Je·hoiʹa·kim when he began to reign, and for eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Ze·biʹdah the daughter of Pe·daiʹah from Ruʹmah.

10202.label: 2 Kings 23:37
10202.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, according to all that forefathers of his had done.

10203.label: 2 Kings 24:1
10203.text: In his days Neb·u·chad·nezʹzar the king of Babylon came up, and so Je·hoiʹa·kim became his servant for three years. However, he turned back and rebelled against him.

10204.label: 2 Kings 24:2
10204.text: And Jehovah began to send against him marauder bands of Chal·deʹans and marauder bands of Syrians and marauder bands of Moʹab·ites and marauder bands of the sons of Amʹmon, and he kept sending them against Judah to destroy it, according to Jehovah’s word that he had spoken by means of his servants the prophets.

10205.label: 2 Kings 24:3
10205.text: It was only by the order of Jehovah that it took place against Judah, to remove it from his sight for the sins of Ma·nasʹseh, according to all that he had done;

10206.label: 2 Kings 24:4
10206.text: and also [for] the innocent blood that he had shed, so that he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and Jehovah did not consent to grant forgiveness.

10207.label: 2 Kings 24:5
10207.text: As for the rest of the affairs of Je·hoiʹa·kim and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the affairs of the days of the kings of Judah?

10208.label: 2 Kings 24:6
10208.text: Finally Je·hoiʹa·kim lay down with his forefathers, and Je·hoiʹa·chin his son began to reign in place of him.

10209.label: 2 Kings 24:7
10209.text: And never again did the king of Egypt come out from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that happened to belong to the king of Egypt from the torrent valley of Egypt up to the river Eu·phraʹtes.

10210.label: 2 Kings 24:8
10210.text: Eighteen years old was Je·hoiʹa·chin when he began to reign, and for three months he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Ne·hushʹta the daughter of El·naʹthan of Jerusalem.

10211.label: 2 Kings 24:9
10211.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, according to all that his father had done.

10212.label: 2 Kings 24:10
10212.text: During that time the servants of Neb·u·chad·nezʹzar the king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, so that the city came under siege.

10213.label: 2 Kings 24:11
10213.text: And Neb·u·chad·nezʹzar the king of Babylon proceeded to come against the city, while his servants were laying siege against it.

10214.label: 2 Kings 24:12
10214.text: At length Je·hoiʹa·chin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he with his mother and his servants and his princes and his court officials; and the king of Babylon got to take him in the eighth year of his being king.

10215.label: 2 Kings 24:13
10215.text: Then he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of Jehovah and the treasures of the king’s house, and went on to cut to pieces all the gold utensils that Solʹo·mon the king of Israel had made in the temple of Jehovah, just as Jehovah had spoken.

10216.label: 2 Kings 24:14
10216.text: And he took into exile all Jerusalem and all the princes and all the valiant, mighty men—ten thousand he was taking into exile—and also every craftsman and builder of bulwarks. No one had been left behind except the lowly class of the people of the land.

10217.label: 2 Kings 24:15
10217.text: Thus he took Je·hoiʹa·chin into exile to Babylon; and the king’s mother and the king’s wives and his court officials and the foremost men of the land he led away as exiled people from Jerusalem to Babylon.

10218.label: 2 Kings 24:16
10218.text: As for all the valiant men, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the builders of bulwarks, a thousand, all the mighty men carrying on war, the king of Babylon proceeded to bring them as exiled people to Babylon.

10219.label: 2 Kings 24:17
10219.text: Further, the king of Babylon made Mat·ta·niʹah his uncle king in place of him. Then he changed his name to Zed·e·kiʹah.

10220.label: 2 Kings 24:18
10220.text: Twenty-one years old was Zed·e·kiʹah when he began to reign, and for eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Ha·muʹtal the daughter of Jeremiah from Libʹnah.

10221.label: 2 Kings 24:19
10221.text: And he continued to do what was bad in Jehovah’s eyes, according to all that Je·hoiʹa·kim had done.

10222.label: 2 Kings 24:20
10222.text: For on account of the anger of Jehovah it took place in Jerusalem and in Judah, until he had cast them out of his sight. And Zed·e·kiʹah began to rebel against the king of Babylon.

10223.label: 2 Kings 25:1
10223.text: And it came about in the ninth year of his being king, in the tenth month on the tenth day of the month, that Neb·u·chad·nezʹzar the king of Babylon came, yes, he and all his military force, against Jerusalem and began camping against it and building against it a siege wall all around.

10224.label: 2 Kings 25:2
10224.text: And the city came to be under siege until the eleventh year of King Zed·e·kiʹah.

10225.label: 2 Kings 25:3
10225.text: On the ninth day of the [fourth] month the famine was severe in the city, and there proved to be no bread for the people of the land.

10226.label: 2 Kings 25:4
10226.text: And the city got to be breached, and all the men of war [fled] by night by the way of the gate between the double wall that is by the king’s garden, while the Chal·deʹans were all around against the city; and [the king] began to go in the direction of the Arʹa·bah.

10227.label: 2 Kings 25:5
10227.text: And a military force of Chal·deʹans went chasing after the king, and they got to overtake him in the desert plains of Jerʹi·cho; and all his own military force was scattered from his side.

10228.label: 2 Kings 25:6
10228.text: Then they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Ribʹlah, that they might pronounce a judicial decision upon him.

10229.label: 2 Kings 25:7
10229.text: And Zed·e·kiʹah’s sons they slaughtered before his eyes, and Zed·e·kiʹah’s eyes he blinded, after which he bound him with copper fetters and brought him to Babylon.

10230.label: 2 Kings 25:8
